The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

Bella’s Pocketful of Thunder

Bella wanted to bring thunder to Everybody Day. “Real thunder may be a bit big for the doorstep,” Daisy said. “Mine will fit in a pocket,” Bella promised. None of the Chirps had a pocket, but that was a small detail.

She wanted to put on a play about a cloud with hiccups. It needed one alarming rumble and three ridiculous ones. She tried rolling a stone across the boards. It went grrrr… and rolled off into a boot.

She tried rattling two sticks. They went clickety-clack. They sounded like a cloud with very good teeth. Mouse stuck out two crumbs like front teeth, and for a while the play was entirely about teeth.

Then Bella stepped on a dry pea pod. Rrrup! She picked it up. Three loose seeds rolled from one end to the other. She tipped it very slowly. Faraway thunder!

“Let me be the cloud,” Mouse said. Bella shook the pod hard. Mouse jumped a whole tail length. “Can I know when the big one is coming?” he asked. Bella thought about the bit of play before a noise.

“Watch my foot,” she said. “When it goes up, the cloud takes a breath.” Up went her foot. Mouse puffed out his cheeks. RRRRUP! His hiccup shot a paper raindrop clean over the front row.

The audience asked to try the thunder. Bella passed the pod along. Toad made sleepy thunder. Caty made tiptoeing thunder. Daisy made thunder that appeared to have forgotten why it came into the room.

Bella drew the pod and its three seeds on a leaf for the Welcome Tree. Then she found a folded scrap of cloth, tucked her thunder inside and tied the scrap to her basket. The thunder had a pocket after all.
